aero.air_density_note: ISA sea-level standard value. Kept at Level 1 by convention like wheelbase_m -- not a sourced-vs-placeholder distinction, a fixed physical constant that would only move for a session weather correction (not implemented).
aero.lift_coeff_sign_convention: cl < 0 means downforce, cl > 0 means lift (standard aero Cl sign; NOT a downforce-positive convention) -- CONFIRMED computationally 2026-08-30 against the live estimate_vertical_loads code, not just inferred from the formula. thesis_notes.md 'Aero downforce sign convention verified computationally'. The FIRST real Cl entry must be negative.
aero.lift_coeff_note: Sign convention verified against the chair's own formula (docs/literature/data_handler.py:1559, fz_aero_total_N = -0.5*rho*v^2*A*Cl, commented 'positive for downforce'): since -0.5*rho*v^2*A is never positive, Cl must be NEGATIVE for a downforce-generating car under this convention -- standard aerodynamic lift-coefficient sign (positive=lift, negative=downforce), not a 'downforce coefficient' convention where downforce would read positive. No numeric Cl default exists in the shared reference files to confirm against directly; this is inferred from the formula+comment pairing alone, not an assumed value. Placeholder 0.0: the aero term evaluates to exactly zero at every speed, i.e. Fz reduces to the static+longitudinal-only estimate -- a documented underestimate of both axles' load at speed, not a front/rear balance error. When populated with a real (negative) Cl, re-verify sign against a high-speed straight-line sample (fz_f_N+fz_r_N should exceed the static sum, not fall below it). This sign convention is INFERRED from the formula+comment pairing, not confirmed against a real value -- the first real Cl entry must be validated empirically (Fz increasing with v^2, not decreasing) before being trusted.
aero.cross_track_area_note: Not sourced -- inert while lift_coeff=0.0 (multiplies to zero regardless). Must be sourced together with a real lift_coeff before either has a numeric effect.
aero.diff_cog_x_note: CoP-to-CoG longitudinal offset. Not sourced, inert while lift_coeff=0.0. 0.0 also has a standalone physical meaning if ever populated alone: aero centre of pressure coincides with CoG, i.e. no front/rear aero balance shift.

stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: CS window floors: cs_min_window_s = 0.1 s, the chair's own value, unchanged. Tested 0.2 s against it on real data (100 Hz grid): same results on all 14 corners, no bootstrap difference -> no reason to deviate. Bootstrap spread measures precision, not closeness to the true tangent; floors chosen by direct validation.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py + inspect_cs_duration_only_comparison.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Exactly the chair's own literal default (10 samples @ their 100 Hz = 0.1s), zero deviation, now that the real fix (PHASE 0's 100 Hz grid) supplies the sample count that default always assumed. A 0.2s hypothesis (double the chair's value, motivated by an a priori 'this car's alpha comes from an ESTIMATED beta -- kinematic or EKF/auto-fit, a noisier Level 1-3 chain -- vs the chair's own MEASURED beta channel, so more averaging seemed plausible') was TESTED AND REJECTED, not just superseded: an isolated duration-only bootstrap (span held at 0.02 rad, cornering-only population) found 0.1s and 0.2s statistically indistinguishable at every tested phase length, and direct real-data Phase 4 validation confirmed the two floors reproduce the SAME worst-lap population almost exactly (identical negative-corner counts, same corners flagged, C4 rear even reads a stronger negative at 0.1s). The plausible-sounding physical story was not supported by either form of evidence gathered -- recorded honestly rather than left implied.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz -- thesis_notes.md) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.2s*20Hz=4 samples would round below a robust minimum; floored at 5 (same magnitude as cs_phase_min_valid_samples's own robustness reasoning), mirroring modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own min_samples_floor precedent (PLAN.md STEP 3, 50 Hz adaptation).
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py, 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Rate-independent (alpha-domain, radians) -- no sample-rate correction applies. Reverted from attempt 2's falsified 0.01 rad back to 0.02 rad (the chair's own original span) after direct real-data validation; unaffected by the separate cs_min_window_s duration question (0.2s vs 0.1s) -- span was never the axis in question there.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: Locality cap for CS window growth, in track metres (state['s_m']), not samples -- same meaning in slow and fast corners. Natural window on corner samples: median 24.1 m front / 35.4 m rear (diagnostics/inspect_cs_max_window_locality_sizing.py); cap = 1.5 x rear median = 53 m. No corner lost at either floor (diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py). The span floor, not min_window, sets the real window size. Limitation: some corner-to-corner gaps are < 53 m, so a window can bridge into a neighbour there. Floors not met within the cap -> NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: Per-phase CS_ratio median -> NaN below this many finite samples. 5 = smallest n where the median isn't just one or two extreme readings. Generic backstop; apex_3 handled by apex_region.
stability_estimation._comment_ls_phase_min_valid_samples: Same gate for ls_ratio_f/r, own key (LS noise differs from CS). Same criterion, same value.
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: entry_1_brake stability stat: same sample-count gate as CS (cs_phase_min_valid_samples), plus no signal if max brake_f_bar never exceeds this floor (no real braking). v3 log_pbrake_f at throttle > 90%: 32829 samples, p99 = 0 bar, one 6.03 bar transient (diagnostics/inspect_v3_brake_phase_stability.py). Real braking phases >= 13.6 bar. 3.0 bar sits between.
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: diagnostics/inspect_cs_window_floor_derivation.py, linear_region_end, 2026-09-02 (CS validity repair part A, Phase 1). Binned the session's own Fy-vs-alpha cloud (both axles, folded to a single sign via the tyre curve's expected odd symmetry, moving & non-kerb samples) with sliding 0.04-rad-wide windows (matched to the re-derived cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad, not an arbitrary narrow bin -- a narrower bin reproduces the same small-span sampling noise Phase 1's own N/span sweeps diagnosed) stepped by 0.005 rad, comparing each window's local slope against the near-origin reference window ([0,0.04) rad). Departure stays within +/-15% of the reference out to ~0.03 rad on both axles, then exceeds 10% and STAYS exceeded (not a single noisy crossing) from window leading edge 0.045 rad (front) / 0.035 rad (rear) onward, climbing to full sign reversal by ~0.08-0.09 rad -- the genuine nonlinear/saturation region. Value set at the more conservative (earlier-onset) axle's sustained-departure point, 0.035 rad, rounded down slightly to 0.03 rad for a safety margin against measurement noise; both axles' own curves are still flat (within a few % of the reference) at 0.03 rad.
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: Common grid = min(target_sample_rate_hz, slowest native rate of the fast CS channels: sclu_yaw_rate, log_asteer, log_acc_y, log_acc_z, lap_distance). On Dubai those are 100 Hz, ecu_speed 50 Hz (diagnostics/inspect_native_channel_rates.py); ecu_speed upsampled linearly (inertia-limited). Below min_sample_rate_hz -> refused, naming the binding channel; exactly 50 Hz -> runs, status 'channel-limited'. Known limits: tyre_model_ekf.pass_1's R was calibrated on the old 50 Hz grid; kerb_dilation_samples, nis_window_samples (nis_gate/tyre_fit_auto/tyre_model_ekf) and apex_half_window_samples are still sample counts -> half their calibrated duration at 100 Hz.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: Which beta feeds Modules 4b/5. Default 'ekf_auto_pacejka' (per-session fit, gated, kinematic fallback). 'kinematic' = estimate_sideslip, the universal fallback. 'ekf_pass_1' = frozen Dugoff curve with calibrated noise (sideslip_ekf_dugoff.py). Traces are fine under any source; verdict thresholds are calibrated for thresholds_calibrated_for_sideslip_source only -> [UNCAL] banner otherwise.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source_auto_modes: 'ekf_auto_dugoff' / 'ekf_auto_pacejka': fit this session's tyre curve (tyre_fit_auto), run the NIS gate, use the EKF's beta_with_fallback only if gate = pass/warn and fit not degenerate; else kinematic, recorded as fallback_used/fallback_reason. Thresholds are never calibrated for these -> [UNCAL] always.
stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: 'static' = estimate_vertical_loads' static/aero/transfer model. 'measured' = wheel_loads cascade (damper -> axle-total reconstruction -> static) for the Fz used by fy_norm and the tyre fit. No damper channels (e.g. Dubai) -> every corner invalid -> cascade returns static everywhere, identical by construction.
stability_estimation.vertical_load_source_derived_from: DEFAULT FLIPPED to 'measured' 2026-09-04 (user decision, Fz-integration package close-out) -- verdict independence PROVEN, not assumed, before the flip: CS_ratio/stability (the only classification/verdict inputs) never receive fz as an argument at all (code-level: estimate_cornering_stiffness/estimate_yaw_moment_stability's own signatures) and both run BEFORE fz is computed in the pipeline; empirically confirmed on Dubai (thesis_notes.md 'Fz-integration Phase 1 (finish): CS_ratio independence...') -- fz_f_N differed by up to 8591.8N between static and measured, but CS_ratio_f/CS_ratio_r/C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r/stability_observed_Nm_per_deg were BYTE-IDENTICAL. The flip therefore carries ZERO classification/verdict risk by construction -- it only changes fy_f_norm_N/fy_r_norm_N (display) and the Phase-2 diagnostic mu tyre-fit's own load input, both already Fz-integration Phase 1/2 deliverables. tests/test_vertical_load_source_default.py (new) confirms the live default is 'measured' and resolves correctly both with real damper channels present (measured cascade engages, every corner tier=damper) and without any (falls back automatically, numerically identical to an explicit 'static' run).
stability_estimation._comment_gps_course_anchor: estimate_sideslip_gps (validation only) anchor gate: smoothed |ay| < max_ay_g for >= min_duration_s. Raw per-sample |ay| gave only ~0.1 s runs; smooth_window_s 0.3 -> 6 runs >= 1.5 s on Dubai. max_ay_g 0.05 ~ moving |ay| p10 (0.044 g), before the rise toward cornering (p20 0.109 g). diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py.
stability_estimation.gps_course_latency_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py, WP5b(c) iteration 1 Section 0: cross-correlation of wrap-safe d(course)/dt against -yaw_rate_radps over lags -1..+1s (racing laps, moving samples) peaks at r=0.9898 at lag=+0.32s, vs r=0.9575 at zero lag -- course-derived rotation consistently lags yaw_rate by this much. A stale course reading recorded at time t describes the vehicle's true state at (t - latency); querying it at (t + latency) recovers the value that actually corresponds to the query instant.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: apex_3 = one instant +/- apex_half_window_samples (11 samples) -- can't clear the CS window floor. apex_region = +/- cs_apex_region_half_length_m around the apex position, used for apex_3 CS reads in classification; apex_3 unchanged otherwise. 25 m = half the ~20-40 m extent of the C4 CS dip -> inside one event, short of the next straight or corner.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); values = the chair's defaults. Changing any of the six means re-deriving the classification thresholds.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback C_linear_ref: axle load x C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad^-1 (Milliken RCVD, GT3 slick). Front (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268, rear (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Level 1. Only used as the fixed stiffness prior of diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py; no production consumer.

nis_gate._comment: NIS tyre-mismatch gate (modules/nis_gate.py; prototype diagnostics/inspect_nis_tyre_mismatch_gate.py). All thresholds PROVISIONAL: gap-selected from five points of one session (one real Dubai fit, four synthetic mismatches); needs more sessions/tracks. Window and band duplicate tyre_fit_auto's so this namespace stands alone.
nis_gate.nis_window_s_derived_from: Morning follow-up bug fix (2026-09-03, damper package Phase 8 continuation -- full record thesis_notes.md 'NIS gate window rate-correction'). SUPERSEDES the literal window_samples=20 key (removed): that value was always a 50Hz-calibrated PHYSICAL duration (20/50=0.4s), silently treated as rate-independent -- once the 100Hz time-base work package moved BOTH Dubai and any 100Hz session onto that grid, window_samples=20 silently represented only 0.2s, HALF its intended duration, for every session this gate has ever evaluated (quantified in the Phase 8 NIS gate redesign proposal, PLAN.md: rate-corrected, Dubai's health_score falls 0.1417->0.1351 and v3's falls 0.1163->0.0849). Same rate-derivation pattern as stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s (modules.stability_analysis.resolve_cs_min_window_samples) and modules.nis_gate.resolve_nis_window_samples now derives the effective sample count from THIS file's own measured sample_rate_hz at runtime, so the window can never again silently mean a different duration on a different grid rate. threshold_use_ekf/threshold_warn are UNCHANGED by this fix -- band/threshold redesign is a separate, still-open decision (PLAN.md NIS gate redesign proposal, Phase 8), deliberately not touched here.
nis_gate.threshold_derived_from: NIS gate redesign, band decision (2026-09-03, thesis_notes.md 'NIS gate band decision: divergence-not-quality redesign'). SUPERSEDES the five-synthetic-data-point gap-selection above (threshold_use_ekf=0.1385/threshold_warn=0.1006): at n=2 real sessions (Dubai, GT3_PRC_MLA-v3) the gate cannot grade fit QUALITY -- there is not enough evidence to say one healthy session's score is 'better' than another's -- so its job is redefined as catching DIVERGENCE only. threshold_use_ekf=0.08 is a round number set below the lower of the two real, live rate-corrected health scores (v3 0.084871, Dubai 0.135131, both re-measured this session via diagnostics/inspect_v3_nis_gate_failure.py) with a small safety margin (~6% below v3), so both real sessions land in PASS. threshold_warn=0.01 gap-selects the FAIL line roughly an order of magnitude below both real scores (8.5x below v3, 13.5x below Dubai) -- reserved for a genuinely collapsed fit (health_score near its structural floor of 0, meaning almost no rolling window ever lands in the healthy NIS-exceedance band), not ordinary session-to-session noise. KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, not re-tested live (tests/test_nis_gate.py's synthetic-mismatch fixture is currently skipped for an unrelated reason, Dugoff degenerating on Dubai under the CS window floor): the WP-N3 synthetic mismatch scenario mu_fz_x2.0 (score 0.0674), which verdicted 'fail' under the old thresholds, would now verdict 'warn' -- an accepted trade-off of this redesign's own stated intent (real n=2 evidence over synthetic-scenario calibration), not an oversight. UPGRADE PATH: a chi-square consistency gate (Kiencke & Nielsen, Automotive Control Systems, 2nd ed. 2005 -- citation TO VERIFY, see PLAN.md ANCHORS) replaces this gap-selected band with a principled statistical test once its own noise-model caveat (R values are themselves gap-selected, thesis_notes.md 'r_q_sweep_note') is resolved or judged acceptable.

Starting point only: a linear KF's gain is provably invariant under uniform (Q,R,P) rescaling, but this EKF's Jacobian is state-dependent (through the tyre model's local slope, which falls toward zero near saturation) and that invariance is NOT assumed to transfer. A same-ratio, different-absolute-scale rerun is proposed as the first sensitivity check, in the validation work package -- not run this pass.

Controlled racing sideslip on this class of car stays well below 15 deg; a genuinely diverged filter exceeds it by orders of magnitude.

pass_0.Iz_provenance: vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2 (2082.0) used in this filter's r_dot, NOT vehicle.yaw_inertia_kalman_kgm2 (1800.0). Chosen because modules/stability_analysis.py estimate_lateral_forces built the Fy_f/Fy_r that this pass's frozen c_alpha/mu_fz were fit against (WP-N1b) using yaw_inertia_kgm2=2082.0 -- using 1800.0 here would make the filter's own moment balance inconsistent with its training data's Iz by ~14%. Both values remain Level-1 estimates/placeholders in their own right (yaw_inertia_kgm2: m*a*b bicycle-model approximation, ~10-20% error, vehicle.yaw_inertia_note; yaw_inertia_kalman_kgm2: unsourced reviewer placeholder) -- 2082.0 is chosen for self-consistency with the training data, not claimed to be the more accurate of the two.
pass_0.fy_axle_dependency_note: Fy_f/Fy_r (estimate_lateral_forces) satisfy a*Fy_f - b*Fy_r == Iz*psidd_raw IDENTICALLY (a=cog_to_front_axle_m, b=cog_to_rear_axle_m derived from the same static corner-weight split as front/rear_fraction; psidd_raw=np.gradient(yaw_rate_radps)) -- verified numerically on Dubai data using a/b computed live from wheelbase*fraction (max abs deviation 7.3e-12 Nm, floating-point noise only). Using the config's own stored (3-decimal-rounded) cog_to_front/rear_axle_m instead gives a small nonzero residual (max 21.1 Nm, mean 5.4 Nm, median relative deviation 0.43% against a 645 Nm floor) fully explained by that rounding, not by any additional independent measurement. Consequence: Fy_f and Fy_r together carry exactly two independent measured quantities (ay and yaw-rate-derivative/psidd), not four independent per-axle numbers -- any fit against both axle forces inherits this coupling, and this must not be read as two independently-corroborating force channels.

R_ay_var/R_yaw_rate_var reflect the completed 2-D sweep refinement (r_q_sweep_note), not just the initial single-shot derivation -- still the same noise-model-only pass, refined in place rather than renumbered, since the tyre curve and Q are untouched throughout.
pass_1.frozen_from: Identical to pass_0 -- copied, not refit this pass. See pass_0.frozen_from for the WP-N1b provenance.
pass_1.seeded_from: Q and P0 copied unchanged from pass_0 -- no non-arbitrary single-shot derivation exists for Q without a Q-focused sweep, still not run (nothing so far implicates Q specifically; see r_q_sweep_note). R redefined to represent TOTAL INNOVATION UNCERTAINTY (sensor noise plus tyre-model error), not accelerometer/gyro precision alone -- pass_0's R assumed 0.05 m/s^2 (ay) / 0.1 deg/s (yaw rate) sensor-only noise while the Dugoff fit's own RMS residuals (WP-N1b) are 2.0/4.3 m/s^2-equivalent per axle, two orders of magnitude larger; trusting the measurement update to sensor precision when the model itself is that wrong is what produced pass_0's 93.4% combined NIS exceedance and the C2 excursion. Full rationale: thesis_notes.md, WP-N2 Q/R recalibration entry.
pass_1.R_ay_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original single-shot derivation (Method A, fit-residual-based, non-circular): WP-N1b per-axle Dugoff fit RMS residuals (front 2752.7 N, rear 5793.2 N over the SAME base_mask population, n=24183) converted to acceleration (front 2.030, rear 4.272 m/s^2). Independence was checked, not assumed: correlation(resid_front, resid_rear) = 0.8999 (materially correlated) -- combined via the correlated formula, giving combined std=6.1516 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=37.8418), vs 4.7197 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=22.2757) under the independence assumption that was checked and rejected. Method B (direct empirical innovation from an actual pass-0 run, std=1.864 m/s^2, R_ay_var=3.475) was measured too but NOT used as the original derivation -- it is contaminated by pass_0's own wrong R distorting the state trajectory; demoted to a post-hoc convergence check instead. That first-derivation value (R_ay_var=37.8418) was RUN and found to over-correct the ay channel (0.04% NIS exceedance, Kalman gain's ay column collapsed ~180x vs pass_0) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.R_yaw_rate_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original derivation, sequenced after R_ay (not simultaneously, to avoid conflating yaw-rate's own model error with a knock-on effect of the ay miscalibration corrupting the shared 2-state update): yaw-rate innovation std was 3.1709 deg/s at pass_0 (R_ay still wrong); after fixing R_ay alone (interim run, R_yaw_rate/Q still at pass_0 values) it dropped to 2.2278 deg/s -- confirming part of the original inflation WAS a knock-on effect, but a substantial independent residual remained. That first-derivation value (R_yaw_rate_var=0.001511889) was RUN and found to under-correct (30.1% NIS exceedance, above the 15% gate) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.r_q_sweep_note: The two single-shot derivations above landed the two channels on OPPOSITE sides of the 3%-15% NIS-exceedance gate (ay too low at 0.04%, yaw rate too high at 30.1%) -- a scalar rescale of R as a whole cannot fix an imbalance between its own two diagonal entries, so a 2-D grid over (R_ay_scale, R_yaw_rate_scale), each independently multiplying this pass's own first-derivation values, was run instead of restarting from scratch (diagnostics/inspect_ekf_pass1_rQ_sweep.py, Q held fixed -- nothing diagnosed so far implicates Q specifically). Of 25 grid points (R_ay_scale in [1,0.3,0.1,0.03,0.01], R_yaw_scale in [1,2,4,8,16]), exactly one landed both channels inside [3%,15%]: R_ay_scale=0.1 (R_ay_var=3.78418, yaw_exceed=10.0%), R_yaw_scale=4.0 (R_yaw_rate_var=0.0060476, ay_exceed=9.2%) -- the values now stored above. Notable cross-check: R_ay_scale=0.1 lands within 9% of Method B's earlier-demoted empirical estimate (R_ay_var=3.475) -- the contamination concern that demoted Method B was real in principle but turned out not to be a large practical distortion for this specific number.

longitudinal_stiffness.brake_front_fraction_fallback_note: Chair performance_analysis tooling's own default_brake_front_fraction constant (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py calculate_longitudinal_axle_forces, internal) -- adopted verbatim, used only when log_pbrake_f/log_pbrake_r are both unavailable/invalid (on this session's data both are whitelisted and valid, so the measured-split path is the one actually exercised).
longitudinal_stiffness.min_window_s_derived_from: LS validity repair (Metrology extension Phase 2a, 2026-09-19, thesis_notes.md 'Metrology extension Phase 2: LS_ratio validity repair'), applying the CS_ratio playbook (thesis_notes.md 'CS validity repair, part A, Phase 1 REVISION') -- SUPERSEDES regression_window_s (renamed: this is now a FLOOR the window adaptively widens past, not a fixed half-window). Method: bootstrap-resampled (B=150) phase-level MEDIAN stability (what summarise_corners's own _stats() actually feeds classify_fn/the frame) vs candidate (n,span), on real kappa/Fx, longitudinal-DEMAND population only (|ax|>1.0 m/s^2, moving, non-kerb), at the shortest MEANINGFUL representative corner-phase length per session (L=20 samples/0.2s -- the real p10 was 2-3 samples on both sessions, physically degenerate for ANY floor choice, excluded from governing the choice the same way CS excluded its own degenerate entry_1_brake case). GOVERNING case (smallest (n,span) clearing P75<=15% relative std, most demanding of 2 sessions x 2 axles): v3 rear axle, (n=40, span=0.016) -- median=0.044, P75=0.123 (diagnostics/inspect_ls_window_floor_derivation.py's own full grid: all other session/axle combinations clear at n<=40 too). 40 samples @ 100 Hz (both sessions' own resolved grid rate) = 0.40s -- notably close to the chair's own literal regression_window_s=0.45s default (a reassuring convergence, unlike CS's own bootstrap-vs-chair-literal tension that was later resolved in the chair's favour; no such tension here, the derived value and the chair's own choice already agree to within 0.05s).
longitudinal_stiffness.min_window_samples_floor_note: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.40s*20Hz=8 samples -- same reasoning as modules.stability_analysis's own cs_min_window_samples_floor (0.2s*20Hz=4, floored to 5); 8 needs no further rounding up since it already clears that same robustness bar. SUPERSEDES min_samples_floor=15 (the pre-repair 50 Hz half-window adaptation, thesis_notes.md 'PLAN.md STEP 3: 50 Hz min_samples adaptation') -- that floor protected a DIFFERENT quantity (half_window+1 under a fixed, non-widening window) which no longer exists as a concept once the window adaptively widens past min_window_s.
longitudinal_stiffness.min_slip_span_derived_from: Same derivation run as min_window_s above (diagnostics/inspect_ls_window_floor_derivation.py) -- (n,span) chosen jointly, not independently, since the bootstrap tests the REAL adaptive-widening mechanism (reconstruct_ls_window_start) at each candidate pair. SUPERSEDES 0.004 (the chair's own literal LongitudinalStiffnessConfig.min_slip_span default, never re-derived for this car until now) -- a 4x increase, the same order-of-magnitude jump CS_ratio's own span floor needed (0.02->0.04 rad in its second pass) for the same underlying reason: the chair's own literal floor sits deep in the small-window overfitting regime for this car's real kappa/Fx noise.
longitudinal_stiffness.max_window_m_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_ls_max_window_locality_sizing.py, 2026-09-19, mirroring modules.stability_analysis's own cs_max_window_m REVISION methodology (natural uncapped window footprint under the just-derived floors, real track distance via s_m, longitudinal-DEMAND samples only). Measured footprint (both sessions, both axles): Dubai front median=61.6m/p90=424.6m/p95=556.7m/p99=830.7m, Dubai rear median=24.5m/p90=171.9m/p95=345.7m/p99=586.0m, v3 front median=111.0m/p90=609.9m/p95=840.2m/p99=1122.0m (the most demanding case throughout), v3 rear median=37.9m/p90=254.0m/p95=447.0m/p99=727.8m. DEVIATION FROM CS's OWN MULTIPLIER, stated not hidden: CS sized its cap at 1.5x its own more-demanding-axle MEDIAN, because CS's own median/p90 ratio was tight (~3x, a naturally compact lateral-cornering footprint). LS's own footprint is far more heavy-tailed (v3 front median/p90 ratio ~5.5x) -- a REAL, physical difference: LS's own domain is longitudinal braking/traction zones, which can legitimately span a much longer track distance at speed than a single corner's lateral extent, not an estimator defect. Applying CS's literal 1.5x-median multiplier here (167m) would have sat BELOW even the p90 of the most demanding case, discarding a much larger share of genuine long-braking-zone signal than CS's own choice ever did to its own data. Sized instead at the P95 mark of the single most demanding case (v3 front, 840.2m), rounded to 900m -- comfortably captures routine real long-braking-zone events, sits clearly below the P99/max multi-event-spanning tail (1122.0m / 5696.9m) that a straight/no-real-signal stretch under a loose |ax|>1.0 demand mask can produce.

longitudinal_stiffness.plausibility_az_window_note: NEW, additive (decided 2026-08-30, user decision). wheel_speed_guard._comment: Wheel-speed plausibility gate (_guarded_wheel_speed_kmh), signal processing only. Per window_s window a log_speed_{corner} is invalid if std < std_min_kmh while moving (stuck) or its mean ratio to the axle mate is off 1.0 by more than ratio_max_deviation (ecu_speed decides which side). Invalid -> abs_speed_{corner} if available, else NaN. Trigger case: v3 log_speed_rr, spurious 300.5 kph peak, > 15% off its mate on 5.9% of moving samples (diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py). Feeds kappa and the LS guard.
wheel_speed_guard.window_s_note: Physical window duration, rate-derived to samples at runtime (same pattern as stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s) -- not independently re-derived this session, chosen as a plausible sub-second fault-detection window matching this project's other window-based guards (NIS gate 0.4s, kerb az windows 0.15-0.6s).
wheel_speed_guard.std_min_kmh_note: Stuck-while-moving floor. FIRST VALUE TRIED (1.0 kph) WAS WRONG, caught empirically before shipping (diagnostics/inspect_wheel_speed_guard_before_after.py's own first run flagged 22-45% of samples on every corner of BOTH sessions, including Dubai's known-healthy channels -- traced to this threshold, not the ratio check, which independently measured only 0.19% false-positive on the same Dubai FL/FR pair): a 0.5s window's real, healthy std is itself often below 1.6 kph (Dubai log_speed_fl, moving windows: p10=0.53, p25=0.91, p50=1.61 kph) -- 1.0 kph sat in the middle of NORMAL variation, not below it. 0.1 kph sits ~5x below that real p10, a genuine margin above true zero-variance rather than a guess -- the ratio-to-mate check is what actually catches real faults (v3's log_speed_rr, thesis_notes.md 'Fz-integration Phase 5...'); this stuck check is a rarely-firing defensive second condition, evaluated only on moving samples so genuine standstill is never mistaken for a stuck sensor.
wheel_speed_guard.ratio_max_deviation_derived_from: Gap-selected against v3's own log_speed_rr/log_speed_rl ratio-deviation distribution (moving samples, diagnostics/inspect_v3_wheel_speed_census.py): the real/plausible population sits below its own p90 (4.62% deviation -- ordinary cross-axle cornering differential and sensor noise), the fault population's own p95 is already 20.40% -- 10% sits in the gap between the two, well clear of both.
wheel_speed_guard.abs_speed_channel_note: abs_speed_fl/fr/rl/rr (config/channels.json, newly whitelisted this phase) are the ABS-domain wheel-speed alternative -- present and 100Hz on BOTH real sessions (v3 unit 'kph', Dubai unit 'mph', confirmed directly per file, same per-file-unit hazard as log_susp_travel/lap_distance -- modules.longitudinal_forces._normalize_wheel_speed_to_kmh converts, never assumes).

wheel_loads._comment: Per-wheel Fz from pushrod force and suspension travel (wheel_loads.py; Segers ch. 9/10). Level 4 per corner where log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are both valid; static split (Level 1) as fallback per corner, never a whole-session switch.
wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_note: Level 1 default (zero). 'Pushrod gauges give absolute force via entered offsets' per the work order -- log_dms_dam_* is already logged in [N] (confirmed from the raw file header, not assumed), so an offset here is a zero-load calibration correction the team would enter after a static gauge check, not a unit conversion. No such session-entered value exists yet anywhere in this project (no UI field, no setup_data key) -- left at 0.0 (i.e. the raw channel is trusted as already zeroed) until a real calibration procedure and entry point exist. Phase 2's straight-line total-load validation is the check on whether 0.0 is a reasonable assumption for this file.
wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_note: Level 1, work-order-supplied figures (not independently sourced this package) -- per-wheel unsprung mass (upright, hub, brake, wheel/tyre assembly, half-shaft share), typical order of magnitude for a GT3-class car. Feeds the unsprung-mass lateral-transfer term, which bypasses the damper/spring entirely (reacts through the upright/tyre contact directly) and must be added on top of the damper-derived sprung force, never folded into it.
wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE, not a measured dynamic (loaded) radius. Derived from the team-supplied STATIC tyre circumference (thesis_notes.md 'Rolling circumference: three disagreeing numbers, none resolved', front 2140mm / rear 2210mm, itself flagged TODO-verify, no datasheet seen) via radius = circumference/(2*pi): front 2140/(2*pi)=340.6mm, rear 2210/(2*pi)=351.8mm. Dynamic (loaded, rolling) radius is normally a few percent smaller than static/free radius under load -- this approximation is NOT corrected for that effect. Used only for the unsprung-mass transfer arm h_u; listed here explicitly as an estimate needing a better source, per the work order's own instruction not to invent precision.
wheel_loads.roll_centre_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE. Read from config/car_data.json kinematic_variants_front/rear's own stated baseline_variant (FS15 front, RS25 rear) roll_center_mm column, converted mm->m -- NOT confirmed against which kinematic variant is actually fitted for the GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 session (no setup record identifies it). Used for the sprung-mass GEOMETRIC lateral-transfer term (the portion of roll-induced load transfer carried through the suspension linkage/roll axis rather than through spring compression) -- this is the only sprung-mass transfer component added on top of the damper-derived force; the ELASTIC portion is already present in the measured pushrod force itself and must not be added twice.
wheel_loads.arb_motion_ratio_approximation_note: Work-order-authorised approximation: no dedicated ARB-linkage motion ratio is digitised anywhere in car_data.json (only 'N/mm at drop link' rate tables plus a scalar ratio_to_wheel). modules/wheel_loads.py approximates the ARB's own travel-to-wheel motion ratio with the SAME damper motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel value used for the pushrod force at that instant (axle-matched) -- an approximation, not a measured ARB kinematic curve, flagged per corner in the module's own docstring.
wheel_loads.arb_position_fallback_note: Level 1 fallback ARB blade position (1-7) used only when no per-corner session setup value (setup_parameters arb_fl/fr/rl/rr) is available for the file being analysed -- GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt carries no setup-sheet record. 4 sits inside setup_parameters.json arb_fl's own recorded typical_window (3-5), a reasonable mid-stiffness assumption, not a measurement of this session's actual ARB setting.
wheel_loads.bump_rubber_note: NEGLECTED (documented limitation, not modelled). No bump-rubber engagement detection or force contribution is included in this estimator -- a wheel deep enough into bump to contact its bump rubber will read an UNDER-estimated load (the rubber's own reaction force is invisible to this decomposition, only the main spring/damper and ARB paths are modelled). config/car_data.json's own bump_stop_curve (cellasto_20mm_40shore) exists but is not consumed here; a future upgrade could use log_susp_travel_* proximity to the bump-stop engagement point to flag (not correct) affected samples.
wheel_loads.aero_front_fraction_note: Level 1 estimate, car-specific but still not a real aero-balance measurement (windtunnel/CFD) -- UPDATED 2026-09-19 (Metrology Phase 3, thesis_notes.md 'Metrology Phase 3: rear axle-total residual decomposition'; PLAN.md BACKLOG item B). Front/rear split of modules.wheel_loads.estimate_session_corrected_axle_totals's own session-fitted aero coefficient c_session (a per-session MEASUREMENT, Level 2 -- this split fraction is the only unsourced part of that correction). SUPERSEDES 0.40 (2026-08-xx, an unmeasured GT3-typical rear-biased assumption, front/rear never actually fit for this car). 0.25 is derived from real per-corner damper data on v3 (all four corners damper-measured since Deepening Phase 2): fitting residual_N = a + b*v^2 independently per corner on straight-line (|ax|,|ay|<0.5) samples gives b_fl=0.178, b_fr=0.214, b_rl=0.604, b_rr=0.573 N/(m/s)^2 (R^2 0.56/0.61/0.91/0.91) -- front_b=0.392, rear_b=1.177, front fraction = 0.392/(0.392+1.177) = 0.25. Cross-session confirmed: Dubai's own independently-fit RL b=0.611 matches v3's RL b=0.604 almost exactly, on a different session with a different straight-line speed range -- the v^2 slope, and therefore this split, is not a single-session fitting artefact. Structural check performed before trusting this at all: modules.wheel_loads's own left/right roll-transfer terms cancel exactly in an axle's total (verified at +0.00 N both axles, both sessions) and axle-total residual correlation with |ay| is null (+0.031/-0.058) -- the v^2 fit this split comes from is not contaminated by a roll/geometric-transfer effect. Single-car, two-session telemetry evidence only, not a substitute for a real aero-balance figure -- still flagged on the engineer questions list (PLAN.md 'Engineer follow-up questions -- damper/wheel-load package') for confirmation against real windtunnel/CFD data. Every wheel_loads reconstruction result that used this split states the value in its own returned dict (aero_front_fraction key).
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_travel_mm_derived_f: Fz-integration Phase 1 (2026-09-03): Sample_Dubai.txt's log_susp_travel_rr found frozen (std=0.101mm, range=3.03mm over the whole session) vs its own axle-mate log_susp_travel_rl (std=5.39mm) and every other travel channel checked on both real sessions (Dubai fl/fr/rl: 5.13/6.52/5.39mm; GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 fl/fr/rl/rr: 4.88/7.01/7.20/4.87mm) -- a real dead/disconnected sensor, not a quiet corner (this file's own log_dms_dam_rr force channel is NOT frozen, std=2031N, so the wheel itself is moving, only its travel POT is not). 1.0mm sits with wide margin above the frozen channel (~10x) and well below every real channel's own std (~5x), a gap-selected floor in the same style as this project's other frozen-value guards.
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_force_N_derived_fro: Fz-integration Phase 1 (2026-09-03). No real frozen damper-force example has been observed yet (every log_dms_dam_* channel checked on both real sessions reads std 1489-2083N) -- this floor is set conservatively low (roughly 30-40x below the smallest real std seen) so it cannot false-flag a genuine but quiet corner, pending a real frozen-force case to calibrate against directly the way the travel floor above was. Same guard purpose: a channel logged 'valid' quality and sitting at a plausible constant value is still dead, and channel_quality_gates' own range check cannot see that (it checks the VALUE, not whether it varies).

corner_trace_display.ls_display_min_ax_mps2_note: NEW, additive (Cleanup/reliability/presentation pass, Part A item A4, 2026-09-01). Display-only mask: the corner-trace LS panel only draws a sample where |ax_mps2| exceeds this bound -- LS_ratio is a longitudinal-stiffness ratio and reads as noise, not signal, while the car is near-constant-speed (cruise/apex-coast), independent of the Phase 0 numerical-instability finding. Value chosen from this session's own |ax_mps2| distribution over the same base racing population as thesis_notes.md section 13's LS_ratio stats (moving & ~kerb & valid-lap racing time, n=24183): p5=0.474, p10=0.947, p20=1.807, median=3.970 m/s^2 -- this track's laps spend most of their time under real braking/traction demand, so even a modest cutoff excludes only the genuinely flat segments. 1.0 m/s^2 (~0.1g) is the standard vehicle-dynamics rule-of-thumb for negligible longitudinal load transfer, sits just above the p10 point of this distribution, and leaves the great majority (89.4%) of racing-time samples display-eligible (still subject to LS_ratio's own finite/masking gates on top). Tier C, no estimator/threshold change -- LS_ratio's own numeric output is untouched, only what the corner-trace panel draws.
corner_trace_display.default_laps_shown_note: NEW, additive (trace-dialog addendum item 2, 2026-09-01). Corner trace default: when opened from an 'All laps' analysis (a single-lap analysis still defaults to just that lap, unchanged), the fastest N valid laps of this corner start CHECKED, the rest start unchecked but available -- avoids a wall of overlapping colours on a corner with many laps by default while never refusing to show more if the user checks them. N=5 chosen as a readable default under the addendum's own 10-colour palette (comfortably below the point where the dash-cycling fallback would ever trigger). Tier C UI default, not a science/analysis parameter.

accuracy_levels._comment: Accuracy per quantity: 1 = config default, 2 = session measurement, 3 = logged sensor, 4 = lookup table. Per node: level (static default tier), source, capped_by ('chained-constant: <name>' = an L1 constant in its derivation; 'provenance-assumption: <name>' = an unverifiable assumption about the channel; null = neither). accuracy_resolution.py resolves leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, steering_ratio) per outing; derived nodes cascade from capped_by -- pure (= input level) or bounded by method_ceiling (e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b). Other nodes stay at their static level regardless of cap.

yaw_inertia_kalman.note: WP-S4 diagnostics-only Kalman sideslip observer candidate (diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py); not consumed by any production Module 2-6 path. Distinct node from yaw_inertia (production, vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2) -- deliberately not chained to it.

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); dynamically resolves to Level 4 (car_data.json steering_ratio_table, manufacturer digitised) when that local-only file is present and the cap allows it -- modules/accuracy_resolution.py. wheel_load_damper.note: Damper package Phase 1 (2026-09-02). Per-CORNER, not per-session: a corner whose damper or travel channel is missing/failed (e.g. GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt's own faulted log_dms_dam_fr) falls back to per_wheel_load_split's Level 1 static estimate for that corner alone, recorded per-sample, never a silent session-wide substitution. Not yet wired into modules/accuracy_resolution.py's dynamic per-session cascade or any UI/pipeline consumer -- same incremental scope as per_wheel_load_split's own phase 1 entry above (estimator + static registry first, consumer wiring deferred).

wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.source: quasi-static heave/pitch axle-total (vertical_load_split's own fz_f_N/fz_r_N) minus the real damper-measured axle-mate (modules/wheel_loads.py reconstruct_missing_corner), used ONLY where exactly one corner of an axle is damper-invalid and its mate is damper-valid -- Segers modal-decomposition method, thesis_notes.md 'FR reconstruction: quasi-static modal decomposition' entry
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.capped_by: chained-constant: vertical_load_split (cog_height_m, aero lift_coeff/cross_track_area_m2/diff_cog_x_m -- the axle-total half of this method), wheel_load_damper (the measured-mate half)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.note: Morning follow-up, damper package Item 2 (2026-09-03). Deliberately registered at the SAME nominal Level 1 as per_wheel_load_split despite using three real sensors -- the accuracy-level system records provenance TIER (what kind of source), not within-tier confidence, and this method's own axle-total term is capped by the same unsourced Level-1 aero/cog-height placeholders per_wheel_load_split already carries. In practice more accurate than a pure static-split guess for the missing corner (it uses a real measurement for 3 of the 4 unknowns instead of 0), but that is a within-Level-1 distinction this registry does not represent numerically. Cascade position: tried AFTER wheel_load_damper (Level 4, that corner's own sensor), BEFORE per_wheel_load_split (Level 1 static-only fallback) -- modules.wheel_loads.combine_with_reconstruction_and_fallback implements the three-tier order. LIMITATIONS (full detail in reconstruct_missing_corner's own docstring and thesis_notes.md): a single-wheel event unique to the reconstructed corner is invisible (the axle-total model has no road-input sensing); the warp/torsion mode ((FL+RR)-(FR+RL)) is unobservable with three sensors and a heave/pitch-only model; both corners of the same axle invalid at once falls through to per_wheel_load_split instead (no reconstruction possible from one equation with two unknowns).
